title: Common heart presentation for embedded finite-field coefficients
statement:
Let X be a Noetherian scheme in universe u and A a finite discrete topological field in Type 0. Use the embedded discrete coefficients and specified realization of [def-sfb-embedded-finite-coefficient-realization], constant-model constructibility of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves and constructibility of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and the coefficient-sized small pro-etale site of [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let R be the constant commutative ring sheaf with coefficient field ULift A on that small site. There are additive equivalences E from embedded discrete internal modules to R-module sheaves and H from intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves to R-module sheaves, such that E is strong monoidal for the existing relative tensor structures, the specified finiteRealization followed by D(H) is naturally isomorphic to D(E), and E(M) isomorphic to H(N) implies that M is constant-model constructible if and only if N is intrinsically constructible. This statement is about modules and the compatibility of their actual derived functors; it contains no Tor-amplitude or boundedness assertion.

Exact Lean assertion:
theorem finiteFieldPresentation
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (A : Type) [Field A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A] :
    letI : HasSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} :=
      CategoryTheory.siteAbelianHasSheafify.{u + 1, u, u + 1} _
    letI : (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} :=
      CategoryTheory.siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective.{u + 1, u, u + 1} _
    let R := ConstantCompletion.constant
      (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} X) (ULift.{u + 1, 0} A)
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (ConstantCompletion.Mod R) := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (Scheme.proEtaleRingModules X
        (Scheme.proEtaleConstantRing X (ULift.{u, 0} A))) := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    ∃ E : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
        (condensedRingObj (discreteObj A) X) ≌ ConstantCompletion.Mod R,
      ∃ H : Scheme.proEtaleRingModules X
          (Scheme.proEtaleConstantRing X (ULift.{u, 0} A)) ≌ ConstantCompletion.Mod R,
        ∃ (_ : E.functor.Additive) (_ : H.functor.Additive),
          Nonempty E.functor.Monoidal ∧
          Nonempty (finiteRealization X A ⋙ H.functor.mapDerivedCategory ≅
            E.functor.mapDerivedCategory) ∧
          ∀ (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
              (condensedRingObj (discreteObj A) X))
            (N : Scheme.proEtaleRingModules X
              (Scheme.proEtaleConstantRing X (ULift.{u, 0} A))),
            (E.functor.obj M ≅ H.functor.obj N) →
            (IsConstantModelConstructible (discreteObj A) X M ↔
              Scheme.IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf X (ULift.{u, 0} A) N)

proof.text: Prove invertibility of the specified finite scalar map by the finite clopen fibre covering, and identify its scalar extension with inverse restriction. Let S denote that scalar extension and I the existing intrinsic realization. Their actual composite is finiteHeartRealization.

Obtain the equivalence of I and an additive H whose composite with finiteHeartRealization is monoidal. Define E as the equivalence (S followed by I) followed by H; its forward functor is literally that composite.

Equivalences are exact. Replace the specified left-derived S and right-derived I by their mapDerivedCategory functors using leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory and rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Whisker these isomorphisms with D(H), then apply mapDerivedCategoryCompIso twice. This gives the required compatibility with the unchanged finiteRealization.

For E(M) isomorphic to H(N), full faithfulness of H lifts the isomorphism to finiteHeartRealization(M) isomorphic to N. Apply finiteHeartConstructibility to M and transport across this intrinsic isomorphism. Restriction to constant scalars and isConstructible_of_iso prove both transport directions, including the empty scheme.
